default.flash.help.esp32.title: Serial connect failed? Try these
default.flash.help.nrf52.title: DFU connect failed? Try these
default.flash.help.esp32.intro: The browser couldn't open a serial link to your device. Work through the steps below in order — most connect failures fall out at step 1 or 2.
default.flash.help.esp32.step1: Confirm the device is plugged into {this} computer with a data-capable USB cable (charge-only cables are a common cause — they enumerate power but not serial).
default.flash.help.esp32.step2: Close any other program holding the serial port — Arduino IDE, PlatformIO, the Meshtastic CLI, or another browser tab running the flasher.
default.flash.help.esp32.step3: Many ESP32-S3 / C3 / C6 boards auto-enter bootloader mode on connect, so you may not need to press BOOT first. Try Connect once; if the chip doesn't respond, use manual bootloader mode (step 4). Some boards (e.g. T-Beam 1W) always need the manual steps.
default.flash.help.esp32.step4: Manual bootloader mode: hold {boot}, tap {reset} (on battery-powered boards: power off, hold {boot}, power on), wait 2-3 seconds, release {boot}, then click Connect.
default.flash.help.esp32.step5: ESP32-C3 with USB-JTAG: swap to a different USB port or bypass hubs — some hubs strip the JTAG interface.
default.flash.help.esp32.step6: Still stuck? Try a different data USB cable and a different port on your computer.
default.flash.help.nrf52.intro: The browser couldn't claim the DFU interface on your device. Unlike ESP32, nRF52 devices (T-1000E / RAK4631) reach the bootloader via a hardware button sequence — not by an auto-reset on connect. Work through the steps below in order.
default.flash.help.nrf52.step1: Confirm the device is plugged into {this} computer with a data-capable USB cable (charge-only cables enumerate power but not USB data — DFU can't claim them).
default.flash.help.nrf52.step2: Close any other program that might hold the USB device — nrfutil, uf2conv, the Meshtastic web flasher in another tab, or a previous flasher session that didn't clean up.
default.flash.help.nrf52.step3: Put the device in bootloader mode: {doubletap} (press RST twice in quick succession). Do {not} hold BOOT — the T-1000E uses the Adafruit UF2 bootloader, which triggers on the double-tap only.
default.flash.help.nrf52.step4: After the double-tap, confirm the device enumerates in TWO ways before clicking Connect:
default.flash.help.nrf52.step4a: A mass-storage volume appears (Finder / File Explorer / mount point) with a name like {vol1} or {vol2} (Adafruit UF2 bootloader).
default.flash.help.nrf52.step4b: A DFU-class USB device is visible to the browser (the picker lists it when you click Connect).
default.flash.help.nrf52.step5: Still stuck? Try a different data USB cable, a different port on your computer (avoid unpowered hubs), or briefly disconnect and reconnect the device before the double-tap.

default.flash.mismatch.esp32.body: The connected chip is a {chip} but the picker says you selected {device} ({arch}) — flashing this firmware to the wrong chip could brick the device.
default.flash.mismatch.nrf52.body: The connected USB device reports VID/PID {vidpid}, but the picker says you selected {device} ({arch}) — flashing this firmware to the wrong USB device family could brick the device.
default.flash.mismatch.action: Return to the device picker and select the correct device — or disconnect this board and connect the one that matches {device}.
